titleStmt.title: Musica per l'eseqvie di Louisa regina di Danemarca

work.title: Musica per l'eseqvie di Louisa regina di Danemarca

event.desc: First performance; performed twice again during the following weeks.

history.p: Though Scheibe and his family had settled in Sønderborg in the southern parts of Denmark, he remained in contact with the musical environment in Copenhagen and played an important role in the newly established musical society (Det musikalske Selskab), participating actively in the concerts during the seasons. Scheibe also composed music for official as well as private events at the court. In December 1751, the popular Queen Louise died in childbirth and Scheibe was commissioned by The Musical Society to compose a cantata of mourning commemorating the queen. The work, which Scheibe wrote in Sønderborg and which was completed in January 1752, received three performances during late February and early March 1752 in the society’s hall in Raadhusstrædet. At the official funeral service on 26 January 1752, Bishop Peder Hersleb held a sermon which later was translated into German by Scheibe (SchW C4:002), music was performed though there is no indication suggesting that it was the present cantata by Scheibe. According to the official documents, the music for the service must have consisted of three parts which the present mourning cantata does not. Later, the work which has been preserved was acquired by C.E.F. Weyse, presumably from the estate of Scheibe.

bibl.author: Adam Gottlob Moltke

annot.p: 'Saa snart Hans Majestet Allerhøyst Selv derpaa indfinder sig i Kirken, begynder Guds-Tienesten med en Sørge-Musiqve, som varer i det Længste 20 Minuter, hvornæst Biskop Hersleb holder en Dansk Prædiken over Esaiæ 38 Cap. 17 v. som varer i det høyeste en Time, derpaa en Sørge-Musiqve af 20 Minuter, hvorefter den første Hof-Prædikant Bluhme, holder den anden Prædiken i det Tydske Sprog over forbemeldte Text og besluttes endeligen Guds-Tienesten med en Sørge-Musiqve af 20 Minuter eller fleere Minuter. Medens den sidste Sørge-Musiqve vedvarer, tilbagebringes, som før er meldt, Hendes Majestæts Crone paa sædvanlig Maade udi det Kongelige inderste Forgemak [...]'

bibl.title: Ved Hendes Majestets, Høysalig Dronning Lovises Henbringelse

annot.p: The review mentions that at the previous concert a German 'Trauer-Cantate' was performed by a learned author (no name is mentioned and neither is the composer). The event was most likely 3 February 1751. One of the text sources is in fact bound with a libretto 'Trauer-Kantate, bey Gelegenheit des am 19 Decemb. 1751. [...] den 3ten Februar, 1752.' (DK-Kk, E 7292 4o); see SchW B7:001.

incipText.p: Rinder i Taarer fra bundløse Floder
Ey noget Torden-Slag kand os saa bange giøre
Ja see! Hvor Skiæbnen har forøget Eders Smerte
Der er fornummet en Røst i det Høye
Bort Leeg og Lyst, og hvad som giver Glæde
Hvad nu? Hvad Graad! Hvad Jammer-Skriig?
See Kongens Datter og Dronning er prydet
See i Fred paakom mig en Bitterhed
Nu sidde vi da og begræde

annot.p: In margin at stave Scheibe has written 'Tenore'; however, he employs the C1-clef indicating a cantus part. The part might have been ascribed to either 'Dyden' or 'Kiærlighed'.

incipText.p: Du Kongers Konge giv vor Konge Fryd og Glæde

titlePage.p: Musica | Per l’Eseqvie | di | Louisa | Regina | di Danemarca | composta di | Giovanni Adolfo Scheibe | Maestro di Capella di /sua Maesta | il Re | di | Dannemarca. | NB. Von der musikalische Gesellschaft in Copenhagen | aufgeführt. | 1752.

physDesc.watermark: the source contains at least two distinct watermarks: 1) fol. 1 has a crowned coat-of-arms of Amsterdam set between two lions (cf. Heawood:415) and the countermark ‘IH’ or ‘HI’ (J. Honig); and 2) on pp. 19−20 the countermark is 'ISRB' which is also found in SchW B2:439 composed summer 1752.
physDesc.physMedium: In 2o, upright format consisting of 4, 4, 4, 4, 3, 4, and 2 nested bifolios; 52 folios, numbered 1−103; title page (on different paper, perhaps once part of a folder; p. 1), blank page (p. [2]), music (pp. 3–102), empty music page (p. 103), empty music page (p. [104]); in all 104 pages. Hand-ruled paper, 22–25 staves (7 mm; single rastrum used) in light brown ink and music in black ink. The front pastedown has in addition to shelf marks been stamped ‘DET STORE KONGELIGE BIBLIOTHEK’ and ‘ BIBLIOTECA REGIA HAFNIENSIS’, ‘63’ added in red crayon, and a label, ‘WEYSES SAMLING | DET KGL. BIBLIOTEK’, pasted on to the front pastedown. A clean copy with only very few corrections or changes, all made in the same ink as the autograph; bar numbers added in pencil, presumably during the production of a new full score in 1943 (‘Egne Afskrifter’).

Paper of a fairly dense quality. New half-binding with the original leather spine, including title and composer’s name gold tooled on coloured paper, pasted on to the new; tightly bound affecting margins.

Paper of an inferior quality. Full-bound, marbled library binding of the nineteenth century.
